dialogue: Could you recommend a 5-day travel itinerary for 2 people starting in Charlotte and visiting 2 different cities in Louisiana from March 9th to March 13th, 2022? Our budget is $1500. We require accommodations that allow parties and offer private rooms, and we'd prefer not to travel by flight.

The other person traveling with me can’t comfortably manage an intercity transfer and needs to stay with me, so please change the trip from two cities to one, base us only in New Orleans, and switch from a private room to an entire apartment. Keeping us together matters more than visiting two cities or having party-friendly lodging, so I’m willing to give up the parties requirement and replan the trip around New Orleans.

Let’s relax the no-flight preference: we’ll drive together from Charlotte to New Orleans on March 9, fly back together on March 13, raise the budget from $1500 to $2000, and reserve that final day for the airport instead of sightseeing, including Mardi Gras World. Getting us home reliably now matters more than avoiding flights or keeping the last attraction.
Since the return flight isn’t available, let’s drive together to Charlotte on March 13 in the same car, checking out early and skipping all sightseeing that day, including Mardi Gras World.
Let’s make simple breakfasts at the apartment and choose sit-down restaurants for lunch and dinner instead of fast food.

My travel companion needs less walking and a seated break between major attractions, so their comfort matters more than fitting in every sight. Limit full sightseeing days to two substantial stops, dropping The Cabildo and The Singing Oak first.
Let’s keep sit-down meals for our New Orleans sightseeing days, but allow packed food or quick-service stops during the long drives on March 9 and 13.

constraints.value: Have simple self-catered breakfasts at the apartment and sit-down lunches and dinners on New Orleans sightseeing days, but allow packed food or quick-service stops during the long drives on March 9 and March 13.
Schedule no more than two substantial attractions on each full sightseeing day; treat The Cabildo and The Singing Oak as the first stops to drop.
Cannot comfortably manage an intercity transfer during this short trip and should remain in the same accommodation with me.
Needs a low-walking itinerary with a seated rest break between major attractions.

agent_action.rationale: The selected entire apartment supports two occupants and its four-night minimum exactly matches March 9–13; at $186 per night it costs $744. Both supported self-drive routes cost $114 total. The listed restaurant average costs sum to $264, producing a known total of $1,122. Groceries, packed meals, attraction admission, parking, and local driving costs are unpriced, so the $2,000 budget cannot be fully verified. The plan keeps both travelers together, uses no intercity transfer, limits sightseeing to two stops per full day with seated breaks, and omits all final-day sightseeing. No active requirement is knowingly unmet.
